title: Coefficient field embeddings preserve independence in a direct sum
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $\sigma:k\to k$ be an injective unital ring homomorphism. Let $I$ be any set, and write $k^{(I)}$ for the $k$-vector space of finitely supported functions $I\to k$, with pointwise addition and scalar multiplication. Define $T_\sigma:k^{(I)}\to k^{(I)}$ by $T_\sigma(v)(i)=\sigma(v(i))$. Let $m\geq0$ and $v_1,\ldots,v_m\in k^{(I)}$. If $\sum_{j=1}^m c_jv_j=0$ for $c_j\in k$ implies every $c_j=0$, then $\sum_{j=1}^m c_jT_\sigma(v_j)=0$ for $c_j\in k$ also implies every $c_j=0$. No surjectivity hypothesis is imposed on $\sigma$. The empty family and empty coordinate set are allowed.

source.place: Agent algebraic refinement supporting Proposition 14.50, printed p.296, and the homogeneous Frobenius-module prerequisite in the vector-group argument. This refinement is not stated in Milne; its independent argument is recorded in the delivery report. No Stacks tag is asserted. Independence argument: applying Frobenius to coefficients in a chosen free-module coordinate system, before shifting the exponent of F.

proof.text: Let $S=\bigcup_{j=1}^m\operatorname{supp}(v_j)$, a finite subset of $I$, and let $u_j=v_j|_S\in k^S$. A relation $\sum_j c_ju_j=0$ extends by zero to $\sum_j c_jv_j=0$, since each $v_j$ vanishes outside $S$. Thus the $u_j$ are independent over $k$. Also $\sigma(0)=0$, so each $T_\sigma(v_j)$ vanishes outside $S$, and its restriction to $S$ is $\sigma\circ u_j$.

source.place: Agent refinement supporting Proposition 14.50, printed p.296; finite support reduction; written here, not asserted in Milne.

proof.text: Put $K=\sigma(k)\subseteq k$. This is a field: it contains $0,1$, is closed under addition, negatives and multiplication by the ring-homomorphism laws, and the inverse of a nonzero $\sigma(a)$ is $\sigma(a^{-1})$, since $a\ne0$. Thus the inclusion gives a field extension $k/K$. Define $w_j\in K^S$ by $w_j(i)=\sigma(u_j(i))$. For a relation $\sum_j d_jw_j=0$ with $d_j\in K$, choose $c_j\in k$ with $d_j=\sigma(c_j)$. For every $i\in S$, the relation reads $\sigma(\sum_j c_ju_j(i))=0$. Injectivity of $\sigma$ gives $\sum_j c_ju_j=0$, hence every $c_j=0$ by step 1 and every $d_j=0$. Therefore the $w_j$ are independent over $K$.

source.place: Agent refinement supporting Proposition 14.50, printed p.296; elementary image-field and coefficient-relation argument; written here, not asserted in Milne.

proof.text: Enumerate the finite set $S$ by $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, where $n=|S|$. Apply [lem-weil-linear-independence-field-extension] to the field inclusion $K\subseteq k$ and the $m$ vectors $w_j\in K^n$ obtained by that enumeration. Its hypotheses hold by step 2, and it permits $n=0$ and $m=0$. Its conclusion makes the images of the $w_j$ independent over $k$. These images are exactly $\sigma\circ u_j$ coordinate by coordinate; returning to the indexing set $S$ merely reindexes the same equations.

source.place: Agent refinement supporting Proposition 14.50, printed p.296; scalar-extension step supplied by the existing Mathlib leaf linearIndependent_algebraMap_comp_iff, Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/LinearIndependent/BaseChange.lean:43-47.

proof.text: Given $\sum_j c_jT_\sigma(v_j)=0$ with $c_j\in k$, restrict to $S$. Step 3 gives $c_j=0$ for every $j$, which is the required conclusion. The argument never chooses a preimage of an arbitrary element of $k$: only coefficients in $K=\sigma(k)$ are lifted in step 2. If $m=0$, the conclusion is vacuous. If $I$ or $S$ is empty, independence of the original zero vectors forces $m=0$ (otherwise the coefficient $1$ at one index gives a nonzero relation).
